title: Bounds and graded pieces of pinned cone filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $K$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, $I$ a bicomplex with complex index $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $r\in\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and $a:K[0]\to I$ a bicomplex map, where $K[0]$ concentrates each $K^s$ in resolution degree zero. Let $b\in\mathbf Z$ and suppose $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ and $K^s=0$ for $s<b$. Let $J$ be the identity-mapped, extended-by-zero and flipped bicomplex [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and let $\epsilon:K\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ be a chain map whose component in degree $n$ is $a^{n,0}$ followed by the extension identification and the $(0,n)$ diagonal inclusion. Set $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon)$, using the mapping cone of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], with canonical inclusions $u_n:K^{n+1}\to C^n$ and $v_n:\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\to C^n$. Let $F$ be any decreasing subcomplex filtration of $C$ [def-sp-filtration] whose degreewise steps satisfy [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] $F^pC^n=(\operatorname{im}(u_n)\text{ if }p\le n+1\text{, else }0)+\sum_{s=\max(b,p)}^n\operatorname{im}(J^{n-s,s}\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\xrightarrow{v_n}C^n)$. The sum is the finite supremum of image subobjects, with empty sum zero. For every integer $n$, $F^bC^n=C^n$ and $F^{n+2}C^n=0$. For all integers $p,n$ there is an isomorphism $H^n(\operatorname{gr}_F^pC)\cong H^{n-p}(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{extend}(a^p)))$, where extend is the resolution-degree extension by zero to $\mathbf Z$. No quasi-isomorphism or injectivity hypothesis on $a$ or $I$ is made.

proof.text: All nonzero I summands on diagonal n have b<=s<=n, and the additional K summand has s=n+1 and is zero if n+1<b. Thus step b contains all nonzero summands and is the whole cone object, whereas step n+2 contains none and is zero. Use the coproduct and cone biproduct universal properties; this includes empty diagonals.

proof.text: Pass to the quotient of step p by step p+1. Projection onto complex-degree-p summands kills all higher summands, and inclusion of the degree-p summands is its inverse on the quotient. Terms of the differential raising complex degree disappear. The surviving resolution differential has coefficient one because J is flipped. On the K^p summand in degree p-1, haug identifies the surviving off-diagonal differential with the extended a^p. These give an isomorphism of the three-term short complex in degree n with the column mapping-cone short complex in degree n-p, also when terms vanish. Apply homology to obtain the asserted isomorphism.
